We just had a bout at the Independence Events Center due to our regular venue being damaged by a storm. It's a nice venue, but the floors were a polished concrete that the Center floods with water and freezes for hockey. Turn two was crazy slick and had a lot of people spilling and two big injuries almost back to back in jams.

Those of you who skate on concrete or have visited a concrete floor, what do you think? Have you had many people who have had problems or injuries on that surface? What do you do to compensate? Best wheels for you?
Polished concrete. Your thoughts on skating it.

I love polish concrete. I'm about 140 lbs and use heartless wheels. My pushers are 88 and the others are 92. They are still really slick and I would probably go a step lower but I love the slide I get. I know a lot of people who pull out poisons when they hear the floor is concrete.
If think I can handle the turns, I stick with my 92s because the slickness helps me slide in to bigger hits. Otherwise, I switch into 88s.

Like I've said elsewhere, I'm a guy, about 170, and I mostly announce and part-time ref. I'm thinking about doing fresh meat again this year and just scrimmaging with the coed teams, so I'm looking to the thoughts of others on floors, wheels, tips, etc.

I have 92s on my skates and I like them, but they feel weird to me when I'm on concrete. After watching the pileups last weekend, it's made me think about 88s if I ever do this for reals. Fortunately our regular floor is wood with some thick coats of paint and I feel good on that surface, but a couple of places our league has skated and could skate are concrete, and reffing one of them was a trip since my wheels didn't grip right. Of course I had even less skate time than I do now.
